issues.description: The answer option (index 2) states '5 revisions are retained' but the explanation states 'Kubernetes keeps the 5 most recent revisions plus the current one' — which totals 6, not 5. These are contradictory. The Kubernetes docs define revisionHistoryLimit as the maximum number of non-current ('historical') revisions to retain. With revisionHistoryLimit: 5, after 8 updates (creating 9 total ControllerRevisions: 1 initial + 8 updates), Kubernetes retains: 5 non-current revisions + 1 current revision = 6 total ControllerRevision objects. The 3 oldest non-current revisions are garbage collected (correct in the option text), but the total retained is 6, not 5 as stated in the option text.
issues.suggested_fix: Change option C text to: '6 ControllerRevision objects are retained (5 historical plus the current); the 3 oldest are garbage collected'. Update explanation to: 'StatefulSets use ControllerRevision objects to track revision history. The revisionHistoryLimit field (default 10) controls how many non-current (historical) revisions are retained. With a limit of 5 and 9 total revisions (1 initial + 8 updates), Kubernetes keeps 5 historical revisions plus the current one (6 total), garbage collecting the 3 oldest. This is analogous to revisionHistoryLimit on Deployments with ReplicaSets.'

issues.description: The verify command 'kubectl get componentstatuses' uses the ComponentStatus API which has been deprecated since Kubernetes v1.19. While the command may still work in K8s 1.29+, it is deprecated and may return incomplete or inaccurate results. The recommended replacement is the livez/readyz API endpoints.
issues.suggested_fix: Change verify to: "kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'" or "kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd" to check etcd health in a non-deprecated way.
